<type>(<scope>): <short summary in the imperative mood>

- <change / implementation detail 1>
- <change / implementation detail 2>
- <change / implementation detail 3>

PR: <full PR URL>
Closes: <full issue URL>

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Squash-merge commit message template (lines starting with `#` are stripped).
#
# Enable locally:
#   git config commit.template .github/commit_template.txt
#
# HEADER (max 72 chars, enforced by commitlint / @commitlint/config-angular)
#   type:  build | ci | docs | feat | fix | perf | refactor | revert | style | test
#   scope: optional, the area of the change, e.g. profile, account, email, ui, deps
#   summary: lowercase, imperative mood ("add", "fix" - not "added"/"fixes"),
#            no trailing period
#   On squash merge GitHub appends the PR number to the header: `... (#159)`
#
# BODY (wrap at 100 chars)
#   What and WHY, not how. Use a bullet list for several independent changes,
#   prose is fine for one coherent change.
#
# FOOTER - every reference as a FULL URL, so the commit stays traceable on its
#   own (`#159` is only a link in the GitHub UI, not in `git log`):
#
#   PR:       https://github.com/gmaster0o0/job-tracker-lite-angular/pull/159
#   Closes:   https://github.com/gmaster0o0/job-tracker-lite-angular/issues/156
#
#   For multiple issues, use one `Closes:` line each.
#   `Fixes` / `Resolves` work the same as `Closes` and also close the issue
#   once the commit lands on the default branch.
#
# RELATIONS (optional, only if there are any - also full URLs):
#   Related:  https://github.com/gmaster0o0/job-tracker-lite-angular/issues/54
#             (related, but does NOT close it)
#   Refs:     https://github.com/gmaster0o0/job-tracker-lite-angular/pull/152
#             (prior art / dependency / earlier part of a series)
#   Reverts:  https://github.com/gmaster0o0/job-tracker-lite-angular/commit/<sha>
#   Follow-up to: https://github.com/gmaster0o0/job-tracker-lite-angular/pull/152
#
# BREAKING CHANGE (if any), in its own paragraph before the footer:
#   BREAKING CHANGE: <what broke and what callers have to change>
#
# Co-author (for shared work), at the very end of the footer:
#   Co-authored-by: Name <email>
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
